title: Greek CH Says K
kidRule: In many words that came from Greek, the letters C and H work together and usually say /k/, just like the K in kite!
hint: This word came to us from Greek, long ago. How do Greek words usually spell the '/k/' sound?
reminder: This word comes from Greek, so the /k/ sound is spelled C-H.

check.question: Why does the CH in ANCHOR say /k/?
check.correctAnswer: The word came from Greek, and in Greek words CH usually says /k/!
distractors: Because CH always says /k/ when it comes after N
Because the H is asleep, so C has to say its own name

words.def: A heavy metal hook dropped into the water to keep a boat from floating away.
words.sent: The sailors dropped the anchor near the sandy island.
words.story: The anchor on a giant ship can weigh more than several cars put together!
words.card: *An* octopus borrowed the ship's *anchor* to use as a fancy hat!

words.def: The part inside your body where food goes after you swallow it.
words.sent: My stomach growled loudly just before lunch.
words.story: Your stomach rumbles when it squeezes air and juices around, and that can happen even when you are not hungry!
words.card: My *stomach* did a happy dance for a bowl of *mac* and cheese!

words.def: The part of a song that you sing again and again.
words.sent: Everyone joined in when the chorus came around again.
words.story: In the plays of ancient Greece, the chorus was a group of people who sang and danced together to help tell the story!
words.card: All of *us* frogs sang the *chorus* until the pond fell asleep!

words.def: A scientist who studies what things are made of and how they mix and change.
words.sent: The chemist mixed two liquids and watched them fizz.
words.story: A famous chemist named Marie Curie discovered two brand-new elements and won two Nobel Prizes!
words.card: The *chemist* made a purple *mist* that smelled like bubblegum!

words.def: A plant with fancy flowers that come in many colors and shapes.
words.sent: A purple orchid bloomed on the windowsill.
words.story: Vanilla comes from the seed pods of an orchid!
words.card: The *orchid* *hid* behind the curtain when the watering can came!

words.def: A person who plans and draws how buildings will look before they are built.
words.sent: The architect drew a house shaped like a shell.
words.story: This word comes from Greek words that mean 'chief builder'!
words.card: The *architect* built an *arch* out of waffles and syrup!

words.def: A person whose job is to fix cars and engines.
words.sent: The mechanic fixed our car so it could zoom again.
words.story: This word grew from an old Greek word for a machine or a clever invention!
words.card: 'Let *me* fix it!' said the *mechanic*, and he gave the car a lollipop.

words.def: A person or animal in a story.
words.sent: My favorite character in the book is the brave little mouse.
words.story: This word comes from a Greek word for a mark that was stamped or scratched into something!
words.card: Every *character* in the play had to *act* like a sleepy sloth!

words.def: A big group of musicians who play many different instruments together.
words.sent: The orchestra played a song that sounded like a thunderstorm.
words.story: In ancient Greece, the orchestra was the round space in front of the stage where the singers danced!
words.card: The *orchestra* kept its tubas in a giant treasure *chest*!

words.def: A lizard that can change the color of its skin.
words.sent: The chameleon sat very still on a leafy branch.
words.story: The name comes from Greek words that mean 'lion on the ground', and its tongue can be longer than its whole body!
words.card: The *chameleon* turned pink when it sat on a slice of *ham*!
